title: Yesterday I… — and verbs that know your gender
title_target: Вчера и завтра — Vchera i zavtra
goal: Talk about what has happened and what will happen, and face one of the most famous traps: Russian past-tense verbs agree with the speaker's gender.
bekal: form past-tense verbs for men, women, and plurals
build future sentences with буду + verb
negate past sentences with не было
tell what happened yesterday, in order

dialogs.title: Диалог — Monday morning after the weekend
dialogs.intro: Марко and Ani swap stories about their weekends. Notice that Ani and Марко use different past-tense endings for the same action.

lines.speaker: Марко:
lines.id: Hi! Where were you on Saturday?
lines.literal: hi! where — you — was (past f) — on — Saturday?

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: I was at home. I worked all day.
lines.literal: I — was (f) — at-home. I — worked (f) — whole — day.

lines.speaker: Марко:
lines.id: I was downtown. I walked around and took photos.
lines.literal: and — I — was (m) — in — center. strolled (m) — and — photographed (m).

lines.speaker: Марко:
lines.literal: very! minus — fifteen. but — was — beautiful.

lines.speaker: Марко:
lines.id: I did. Then I drank hot tea for two hours.
lines.literal: froze. then — drank (m) — hot — tea — two — hours.

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: I didn't have time to go out. The exam is on Friday.
lines.literal: at — me — not — was — time — to-stroll. exam — on — Friday.

lines.speaker: Марко:
lines.id: Oh no. So what will you do this weekend?
lines.literal: oh. then — what — you — will — do — on — weekend?

lines.speaker: Ани:
lines.id: Sleep. For a long time. Then eat. Then sleep again.
lines.literal: will — sleep. long. then — will — eat. then — again — sleep.

lines.speaker: Марко:
lines.id: Great plan. I'll be cooking. Come over.
lines.literal: excellent — plan. I — will — cook. come.

notes: **Past-tense verbs agree with the gender of the doer, not the pronoun.** ⚠️ This is the most famous beginner trap in Russian. The endings: **-л** (masculine singular), **-ла** (feminine singular), **-ло** (neuter), **-ли** (plural). A woman who says *я был* immediately sounds wrong — it should be **я была**. Notice that я, ты, and он all take -л if the doer is male; the pronoun doesn't decide.

**Forming it is very easy: drop -ть, add -л/-ла/-ло/-ли.** работа**ть** → работал, работала, работали. дела**ть** → делал, делала, делали. говори**ть** → говорил, говорила, говорили. Almost no exceptions — much easier than the present tense with its six endings.

**Быть (to be) is absent in the present tense, but REQUIRED in the past.** *Я студентка* (now, no verb) but *Я **была** студенткой* (back then). *Я дома* but *Я **был** дома*. ⚠️ Leaving out был/была in a past sentence is a mistake; verbless sentences only work in the present.

**Было is used in sentences with no subject.** *Было холодно* (it was cold), *Было красиво* (it was beautiful), *Было трудно* (it was hard). The neuter form **было** is used because nobody and nothing is the doer — like English "it."

**Saying something didn't exist in the past uses не было — always the neuter form.** *У меня **не было** времени* (I didn't have time), *У неё **не было** денег* (she didn't have any money). ⚠️ Even if the missing thing is feminine or plural, the form stays **не было**, and the noun goes into the genitive. Compare the positive sentences, which change: *У меня был**а** книга*, *У меня был**и** деньги*.

**The future is built with буду + the dictionary form.** *Я **буду** работать* (I will work), *Я **буду** спать* (I will sleep). This буду is exactly what you used to order in the café in Unit 8. Endings: буду, будешь, будет, будем, будете, будут.

**Замёрз is the irregular past of замёрзнуть (to freeze).** Some verbs drop -л in the masculine form: замёрз (not замёрзл), мог (could), шёл (walked). The feminine and plural forms are normal: замёрзла, могла, шла.

grammars.title: The past tense — one rule, four endings
body: Drop **-ть** from the dictionary form and add the ending that matches the doer's gender and number.
after: ⚠️ Notice how the stress moves in быть: **был** (BYL) but **была** (by-LA), **было** (BY-la), **были** (BY-li). Only the feminine form is stressed on the ending. This odd pattern shows up in some other short verbs too: жил / жи**ла**, пил / пи**ла**.
To negate: put **не** in front, as usual. *Я не работал вчера.* — I didn't work yesterday.

grammars.title: The future with буду
body: The helper verb **быть** in its future form, followed by the dictionary form of the verb.
after: Буду is also used on its own, with no other verb, meaning "will be": *Я буду дома в семь.* — I'll be home at seven. *Завтра будет холодно.* — It will be cold tomorrow.
⚠️ Russian has a second way to talk about the future, using perfective verbs (*Я сделаю* — I'll get it done). That's covered in Unit 20. For now, **буду + verb** always works and is always correct.

blocks.title: The most common past-tense phrases
items: **Где ты был? / Где ты была?** — Where were you? (to a man / a woman). One of the most common questions, and one of the places where gender mistakes are heard most often.
**Я не знал / Я не знала.** — I didn't know. A lifesaver phrase to learn in both forms.
**Извините, я опоздал / опоздала.** — Sorry, I'm late.
**У меня не было времени.** — I didn't have time. Notice **не было**, which never changes.

exercises.prompt: Put the verb in the past tense to match the doer.
Change to the future with буду.
Put the words in the right order.
Translate into Russian. Watch the speaker's gender.
items: Where were you on Saturday? (to a woman)
I was at home. (a woman speaking)
Tomorrow I'll sleep for a long time.
